tob_columba.text: St Columba came here from Ireland in 563, with twelve companions, and built a monastery of wood and wattle. The abbey you see is much later, from the 1200s, but the island has been holy for over fourteen hundred years.
Kings of Scotland were buried here for centuries, including, they say, Macbeth. A nice bit of good press for a man usually described as a murderer.
Iona's called the cradle of Scottish Christianity. Also of Scottish tourism. Please don't picnic on the graves.

tob_pilgrim.text: I walked the island from the jetty. The beach on the south end has little green stones, a marble that's local. People pick them up and carry them home.
The abbey's open till five. Don't dawdle, the last boat leaves shortly afterwards, and the skipper doesn't wait for dreamers.
